text:
anna: quick follow-up from the ACPD RFC review — we need to lock on the operator contract for chunk acknowledgment patterns. thinking about 2 approaches

raj: +1, thanks. can you summarize tradeoffs?

anna: short: 1) synchronous ACK per chunk (simpler semantics, higher latency/backpressure across store-and-forward links) vs 2) optimistic streaming with periodic manifests and per-chunk checksums (better throughput, more complex recovery)

maria: leaning to optimistic streaming + manifests. in air-gapped sites we want minimal round trips. recovery complexity is mostly local agent work.

dave: devil's advocate: if a site loses power during a multi-gig patch, optimistic approach needs robust resume. do we have off-by-one hazards in KV index?

anna: good call. proposal: each chunk gets a monotonic sequence + merkle-prefix in the manifest. resume works by asking for first-missing-seq. no global reapply.

raj: how do we sign manifests? remember compliance wants auditable chain and HSM integration in Private deployments.

maria: manifest signed with customer KMS key (we support HSM-backed signing). operator verifies chain before activation. upgrade-bot: automatic note — manifest size remains small (<<1% of payload) if we use per-chunk 32B hash entries. :white_check_mark:

dave: OK. what about telemetry / metrics for partial-delivery health? we need to show progress to Console (for on-prem customers that have a control-plane connection) and to local operators via CLI otherwise.

anna: propose dual sink metrics: 1) push compact progress events to control plane when available, with signed proof-of-delivery, 2) local metrics file (JSONL) for disconnected environments. format: {"seq":<n>,"status":"applied|pending|failed","ts":<unix>}

raj: agree. also include periodic checksums (every 1000 chunks) so verification is O(1) per checkpoint.

maria: UX question: rollback windows. can we include a reversible activation marker that operator can flip within N minutes? we shouldn't require a full bundle rollback for tiny mistakes.

dave: make activation a two-phase: apply -> staged-verify -> commit. commit toggles active manifest pointer. rollback flips pointer back and triggers garbage-collect TTL. keeps blob store idempotent.

anna: exactly. tradeoff: increases on-disk temp by ~bundle-size for window duration. recommend default 15m window for Dedicated customers, 60m for Private (ops control).

raj: what about signature freshness? if operator flips commit after N minutes, do we re-check signatures vs revocation lists?

maria: yes — revalidate on commit, check CRL/ocsp if available. offline sites fallback: check signature timestamp and local allowlist of signing keys. doc needs to explain legal tradeoffs.

upgrade-bot: note — adding a reconcilier endpoint will be required for Dedicated-to-Private sync. see rfc-acpd-ops-001

anna: next ops item: define API surface for agent -> control-plane checkpoint exchanges. lightweight proto with: chunk_seq, chunk_hash, manifest_id, applied_ts, evidence_sig. I'll draft API and share in a follow-up.

dave: any objections to using gRPC over mTLS for that when available? avoids fragmented HTTP semantics.

raj: gRPC + mTLS recommended, but keep a plain HTTPS fallback for weird proxies. add wire-version header so older agents can be refused explicitly.

maria: sounds good. one last callout: we must document upgrade size limits and an explicit streaming-mode flag so customers can opt into optimistic mode. default to conservative ACK-per-chunk for first 3 rollouts in a new customer environment.

anna: agreed. i'll open a PR for the operator contract and the API proto, set to draft. tagging: @raj @maria for compliance + ops review. :memo:

raj: thx — will review this afternoon.

maria: will test mental model against the on-prem testbed next week.

dave: i'll prototype resume logic in a small repo and report perf numbers.

anna: great. closing thread for now — will ping when PR is up. :sparkles:
